column3: What is the largest ocean on Earth?

column3: Which line of latitude divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?

column4: City A, because temperature drops with altitude
column8: Britannica lapse-rate gives the ~6.5 C/km environmental lapse rate in the lower atmosphere.

column3: Why do places near the Equator stay almost the same temperature all year, while places near the poles have big seasonal changes?
column4: The Sun's angle overhead changes much less near the Equator through the year
column8: NASA Space Place: Earth's tilted axis causes the seasons and changes which parts receive the most direct rays through the year; the equator-vs-poles contrast follows directly.

column3: What is the capital city of Japan?
column8: Britannica: formerly Edo; became the capital after the Meiji Restoration in 1868.

column3: On which continent is the Sahara Desert?

column3: How many hours of sleep do most teenagers need each night?
column8: CDC: teens 13-18 need 8-10 hours per night.

column3: Why is washing hands with soap better than washing with water alone?

column8: CDC: soap lather forms micelles that trap and remove germs, chemicals and dirt, better than water alone; the explanation's 'oils' wording is not on the cited page.

column3: Which vitamin can the body make when skin is exposed to sunlight?
column8: MedlinePlus: body forms vitamin D naturally after sunlight exposure; needed for bones.

column3: Which of these foods is a good source of vitamin C?
column8: MedlinePlus: citrus is a good vitamin C source and it helps absorb iron; the explanation's 'supports the immune system' claim is not on the cited page.

column3: How much moderate physical activity should teenagers aim for each day?
column8: WHO: children and adolescents should do at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity daily.

column3: Which drink is the best everyday choice for hydration?

column3: Which blood cells help the body fight infection?

column3: Lentils are mainly a source of which nutrient?

column3: Which hard part of the body protects the brain?

column3: Which vitamin helps the blood to clot after a cut?

column3: Which mineral from milk and cheese keeps bones and teeth strong?

column3: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
